Ralph (Mary Grace Canfield) becomes enamored of Mr. Kimball (Alvy Moore), the county agent. However, though she feminizes herself and gets all gussied up, he refuses to go out with a girl named Ralph. Can Oliver solve the situation legally?

Six months is up! Now, Lisa (Eva Gabor) gets to decide whether she and Oliver (Eddie Albert) will remain on the farm or go back to New York and their Park Avenue lifestyle! Will this be the final straw for Green Acres?

Sam Drucker (Frank Cady) is leaving on a much-needed two-week vacation and talks Oliver (Eddie Albert) into assuming his duties as deputy sheriff. But Oliver soon learns enforcing the law isn't quite as easy as it looks.

Whatever you do, don't say her name and especially while playing checkers down at Drucker's! An old hag named Molly Turgiss (Renie Riano), who died twenty years before the Douglases (Eddie Albert, Eva Gabor) came to town, might be haunting them.

It's a few days before Oliver (Eddie Albert)'s birthday, and Lisa (Eva Gabor) doesn't know quite what to get him�until the old Hoyt Clagwell goes kerflooey! So, she goes out and buys the biggest and fanciest tractor she can find.

Oliver (Eddie Albert) discovers that Eb (Tom Lester) has a way with sick animals after Eb cures Arnold, the pig, and Alice, the chicken, and offers to put him through veterinary college. But will life in Green Acres ever be the same without Ed?!

A horse follows Oliver (Eddie Albert) home, but every time he tries to show it to his wife, the horse disappears. Lisa (Eva Gabor) assumes that her husband is imagining things�and as more animals show up, Oliver begins to think so too.

Mr. Haney (Pat Buttram) takes Oliver (Eddie Albert) to Pixley Superior Municipal Court and sues him for non-payment of a vital contract over the little matter of some rain�or lack thereof. Does Mr. Haney know who he's up against? Does Oliver?

The Third-Tuesday-of-Every-Month-Culture-Committee of the Every-Other-Wednesday-Afternoon-Discussion-Club decides that Hooterville needs some "culture" in the form of a symphony orchestra. And Lisa (Eva Gabor) may just know the perfect conductor.

Oliver's (Eddie Albert) nephew Charles (Don Edmonds) arrives for a visit, and Oliver is completely shaken up when the boy turns out to be a long-haired, motorcycle-ridin', hippy-dippy type. But, boy, does he know a thing or two about engines.

Oliver dreams of entering his crop in the Corn Festival, but the dreaded "Bing Bug" invades Hooterville's farms. After learning of his service as a WWII pilot, the locals volunteer him for the perilous task of flying the town's only crop duster.

When a lovely, young and successful farmer comes to Oliver (Eddie Albert) for his legal counsel, Lisa (Eva Gabor) quickly becomes jealous of the two spending time together and becomes determined to break up what she sees as a budding romance.

When the Monroe Brothers show up to fix the Douglas's closet, Lisa learns that Ralph is devastated because her true love has stood her up on another date. Lisa's solution: an intensive, two-day beauty treatment for Ralph�and the barn for Oliver!

Oliver (Eddie Albert) takes to his soap box, delivering fiery, patriotic speeches after getting a bill from the State Farm Unattached Duty Tax for an outrageous $12.03! But no one can figure out why the tax is levied in the first place.

Lisa (Eva Gabor) is curious to learn about the book that Oliver (Eddie Albert) is reading. It is the "real-life" story of pioneers Gus and Etta Thompson. The episode flashes back to the 19th century with Oliver appearing as Gus and Lisa as Etta.

Eb (Tom Lester) seeks dating advice from the Douglas's after laying eyes on former classmate Betty Jo Bradley from "petticoat Junction." Oliver's well-intentioned guidance has mixed results when Eb hilariously misconstrues the advice he's given.

The locals complain that Oliver's penchant for wearing business suits to do farm work is ruining Hooterville's image. Oliver tries to adjust, but the last laugh is on him when Lisa has her dressmaker design Italian him some swanky new overalls.

The Hooterville Chamber of Commerce attempts to attract a Hollywood film studio to shoot a movie in town. And when a rumor spreads that famous actor is arriving, the townsfolk are all abuzz as they prepare for their close-up, Mr. DeMille!

Fed up with the house being in dire need of repair, Lisa demands that Oliver arrange to have the house redone or she's moving back to New York. Oliver agrees, but is delayed when Mr. Haney claims that their farmhouse is a historic monument.

Everything is topsy-turvy and henhouse hijinks ensue when one of the Douglas' hens is found to be laying square eggs! News of this kind gets around quickly, and the townsfolk all get in on the race to capitalize on the impressive novelty.

Oliver is absolutely determined to have a truly old-fashioned Christmas, including decorating his own farm-grown tree. But warm weather stands in the way and, he discovers, the residents of Hooterville aren't exactly as traditional as he thought.

In true Hooterville fashion, Oliver (Eddie Albert) discovers that the town is vehemently split as to which weather reporter they trust. As debates rage over which forecast is correct, Oliver plants his tomato crop, hoping for the best.

After another disastrous effort from Lisa in the kitchen, Oliver implores her to take a home economics class at the local high school. Before she knows it, Lisa is a fully enrolled student...the likes of which Hooterville High has never quite seen.

When the Hooterville City Council appoints Oliver (Eddie Albert) to judge the apple competition at the annual fair, he mistakes the honor for a real judgeship and prepares for his time on the bench! But a run-in with the real law clarifies matters.

Lisa visits Oliver's mother who is recovering from an illness. The doctor advises that she rest in a peaceful environment...and thinks that Hooterville sounds absolutely ideal! Of course, he doesn't know Hooterville, where peace is never�very close.

When Oliver (Eddie Albert) discovers that Hooterville has a still-valid contract to build war planes, he spearheads the opening of new government defense plant. But as chaos ensues, Oliver soon wonders if the move was a big mistake after all.

Lisa is appointed as head of Hooterville's new "Human Humane" committee. A perfect fit for animal-lover Lisa, and a relief from her boredom in the countryside, she soon has a menagerie of both farm and exotic animals living at Green Acres.

Oliver takes Lisa along to an agricultural convention. There, Lisa bonds with an ex-gangster couple, who insist upon teaching the Douglas's some of their shortcuts to successful farming. It turns out to be an offer that Oliver can not refuse.

Oliver champions agri-tech as way to increase productivity on the farm, but when a computer gives its assessment of the Douglas' marriage, Lisa (Eva Gabor) begins to question her union with Oliver. It's bits versus bytes in Green Acres!

Determined to teach his spendthrift wife Lisa how to save money, Oliver insists that she learn about farming...by growing her own vegetables! In her own inimitable fashion, armed with useless pamphlets from Mr. Kimball, Lisa sets to tilling!

When handyman Eb (Tom Lester) reports he has seen little green men piloting flying saucers, everyone in Hooterville takes him at his word�even the Air Force�and soon the Douglas farm becomes the Roswell of the greater Pixley area!

Ralph (Mary Grace Canfield) is distraught when her beloved Mr. Kimball, is fired as the county agricultural agent. Out of a job, Kimball (Alvy Moore) no longer has money enough to marry the lady-carpenter-in-waiting! But wait�did he even want to?

Lisa weaves the tale of her great, great grandmother, the Queen of the Gypsies, to explain a bizarre family tradition: a woman in her family must marry an American -- but only every fourth generation -- in order to gain a special inheritance.

After Oliver (Eddie Albert) accidentally drops a hammer on her head, Lisa (Eva Gabor) develops a case amnesia, with no idea who she is or why she is on a farm in Hooterville�and she adamantly refuses to believe that Oliver is her husband!

Nothing gets done on the Douglas farm when Oliver (Eddie Albert) gifts Eb (Tom Lester) a top-of-the-line radio for his birthday. Letting nothing stop him, Eb (Tom Lester) enters a radio contest...even when Eleanor the cow swallows the radio whole.

It's a very official third season premiere for Green Acres when the retirement of a state senator leaves Hooterville considering its best candidate for the job. Of course, they turn to their beloved lawyer-come-farmer Oliver Douglas (Eddie Albert).

Oliver finds himself in a jam after asking Lisa to make him homemade fruit preserves. An episode deliciously devoted to Lisa's culinary escapades, Lisa musters all of her Hungarian might to make Oliver the best peach jam he's ever tasted.

After years of substandard service, Oliver is hellbent on throwing the book at the Hooterville Phone Company. When it becomes clear that the local utility oversight board can't do much about it, he decides to handle matters directly.

Mr. Trendell, the president of the Hooterville Phone Company, hands the company over to a delighted Oliver. But after a day of crossed wires and a switchboard repairman with some lose connections of his own, Oliver is ready to call it quits.

For the first time, Oliver has a successful crop that needs picking. His tomatoes have grown beautifully. But matters at the phone company continue divide his precious time, so Oliver looks for an interested buyer to take the company off his hands.

Being president of the Hooterville Phone Company has been a rude awakening for Oliver. The switchboard operator is now calling him at five in the morning! After a bevy of new complaints from unhappy customers, Oliver has just about had enough.

One might think that when Eb takes a vacation things around the farm might go more smoothly. But when Eb elopes, leaving his cousin Walter to take his place, it turns out to be a horrible idea. Walter barely knows a weed from a hole in the ground!

Lisa is reminded that she stored a birthday present for Oliver years ago: a genuine Stavinsky. But what is it? It's a modern art sculpture that is two parts plumbing pipes, one part tire chains, and one part birdbath. Oliver calls it "The Thing."

The continually evolving story of how Lisa (Eva Gabor) and Oliver (Oliver) fell in love gets yet another version in this delightful episode. But one thing is for sure: Lisa and Oliver are just as in love today as the day when he fell out of the sky.

Green Acres is greener than ever, with jealousy. When Oliver (Eddie Albert) hires a handsome, young, intelligent Brit to take over his farm work while he is away, it doesn't take long for the newcomer to make a strong impression on Lisa (Eva Gabor).

Mr. Haney is up to his money-making schemes again. When a government representative tells Mr. Haney that the state is looking to purchase the Douglas farm for a new highway, Mr. Haney arranges to buy back the farm from the Douglases at a steal.

Ralph, the lady carpenter, runs away from home and stays with the Douglases after having a fight with her brother, Alf. While Oliver may never get his bedroom finished, he gains a maid as Ralph takes over as the Douglases' live-in housekeeper.

Picking apples while on a picnic, Oliver runs into the feisty Ira Hatch, the owner of the apple orchard. However, once back in town, Mr. Drucker tells Oliver that Hatch has been dead for years. An incredulous Oliver agrees to see a psychologist.

After his elopement and cross-country honeymoon, Eb returns to Hooterville. But his new wife is nowhere to be found! After sending postcards from all across the country, Eb has to confess that his fianc� stood him up at the alter on their big day.

Someone has stolen $300 from Mr. Drucker's general store, and it looks like Eb is the culprit. How else could he have bought himself a new car that cost, you guessed it, exactly $300? But that is just the first twist of the many turns of this story.

Lisa awakes, saying she's dreamt that she must invest in copper. When Oliver turns that idea down, she seizes on the opportunity to invest in a ten-year-old genius's electric company. Twenty-eight dollars buys her a third of the business.

Arnold, the Ziffels' television-loving pig, has taken on a paper route to save enough money for a new color set. But when bank robbers show up and threaten his dreams, and Lisa and Oliver are held captive in their own home, Arnold has to fight back.

The farmers of Hooterville are headed to France! Or at least they are if they can get organized. As part of an agricultural exchange program, the farmers are offered a chance to join a chartered government flight to Europe.

Lisa (Eva Gabor) is delighted to learn that her Hungarian mother is planning a visit to their little farm. Much to Oliver's (Eddie Albert) disbelief and dismay, a rumor spreads all around Hooterville that Lisa's mother is a European countess.

Love is in the air as the first day of spring arrives in Hooterville. And who better to lead the town in celebrating it than Lisa. She is resolved to show Oliver just what spring is all about and sets out to produce a Spring festival celebration.

It's a hair-raising episode as Eb (Tom Lester) enrolls in a correspondence course to become a barber. Lisa (Eva Gabor) and Oliver (Eddie Albert) give him the money to learn the trade but learning how to cut hair by mail has its glitches.

For a lawyer, Oliver should be more careful about what he signs. Lisa reminds him that two years ago Oliver made her a promise to take her back to New York for a two-week vacation. And she has it in writing� on the bottom of the kitchen drawer.

It's hard to know who has a curse over Oliver, but he sure has his hands full with Lisa and her fellow Hungarian Lazlo Broslav. Lazlo appears with a letter claiming he once saved the life of Lisa's uncle, and now her family must repay the debt.

There's a problem in Hooterville: no farmer seems able to grow a cash crop on account of the quality of the soil. But as it turns out from Oliver's (Eddie Albert) soil and mineral research, the oft misunderstood rutabaga is an ideal choice.

Green Acres goes Hollywood in this first installment of a two-part season finale. When Arnold the pig appears in a play at the Hooterville Theater, Lisa (Eva Gabor) arranges for an old friend to give Arnold a chance on the big screen.

It's a swine-sational third season finale for Green Acres, as Oliver and Lisa chaperone Arnold, the Ziffel's talented pig, to Hollywood for his big screen test. There's only one problem, Lisa failed to mention that Arnold is not your normal actor.

Hooterville is abuzz as the townsfolk enter a contest sponsored by Peterson's Poi Juice, with a trip to Hawaii as the top prize. But no one expects the winner to be Arnold, the Ziffels' talented pig. Maybe a pig might fly after all, to the islands!

A charity rummage sale asks for donated clothing. Being among the wealthier residents of Hooterville, the organizers look to the Douglases. It isn't long before Oliver has to stop Lisa from giving away his entire wardrobe!

Love is in the air when Eb is quickly engaged to Loreli Appleby, whom he has only known for a day. Eb tries to impress Loreli's father, a farmer, but in typical fashion, he accidentally ruins his future father-in-law's cabbage crop.

When Fire Chief Joe Carson is looking for a way to go to Miami, he hires Oliver as his assistant, hoping Oliver will pay for the trip. The plan backfires, no pun intended, when Oliver starts pointing out what a poor job the chief has been doing.

The highways in Hooterville are in dire need of repair. Oliver is fed up and believes he can make a difference by complaining to his state representative, Ben Hanks. But Hanks' popularity proves greater than his sense of responsibility.

Lisa feels like she should be contributing more and wants to start working in Oliver's construction business. Lisa is like a fish out of water as she arrives to the Monroes' workshop in overalls and causes one problem after another.

Lisa plays bovine matchmaker when Oliver and Lisa decide it is time for their female cow, Eleanor, to start providing milk for the farm. Oliver makes arrangements for Eleanor to mooooove in with the neighbor's bull, but Lisa has other ideas.

The townsfolk look forward to "Old Mail Day", when once a year undelivered mail is handed out. The delayed mail includes a letter all the way from 1917! Oliver is upset by the poor service, but his complaints land with more impact than he intended.

When word spreads that an agricultural student is coming to Hooterville to study with county agent Hank Kimball, no one seems to be interested. However, things change when the folks discover that the student is an attractive blonde.

This episode tells the unusual tale of Hooterville's founding. As the town prepares for its centennial, Oliver announces a reenactment of the town's origins and casts himself and Lisa in the roles of Horace and Doris Hooter.

When a blue feather arrives in the mail for Lisa, her Hungarian roots tell her that trouble is brewing. The feather is a symbol of malfortune to come, and she suspects it was sent by Hungarian gypsies, a warning that they are out to get her.

Don't count chickens before they hatch! Oliver thinks he's laid a gold egg of an idea when he decides to dive beak first into the business of raising chickens. Lisa, on the other hand, sees little difference between raising chickens and children.

All that glitters is not frosted cereal. After a jewelry heist in Chicago, the robbers foolishly stash their booty in the grain bin of a cereal manufacturer. Oliver and Lisa discover the jewels in their bowl of Crickly Wickly!

Oliver Wendell Douglas returns from farm to firm... law firm, that is. When a young and ambitious local graduates from law school, he looks for a potential partner in Hooterville. Oliver is the logical choice. Lisa and Eb help the new venture.

After partnering with a young, local lawyer, Oliver has opened a new law office in Hooterville. However, their secretary, Lisa, shows a lack of necessary skills. Soon, Lisa's job is on the line, even if she is married to one of the partners.

When the Young Peoples Agricultural Society holds their annual convention in Washington, D.C., local members Eb, Mr. Kimball, and Arnold the pig get ready to make the big trip. Oliver and Lisa serve as unintended chaperones.

While Lisa and Oliver consider what to do on their unplanned trip to Washington D.C., Mr. Haney rents their house to a family of eight. Meanwhile in the nation's capital, Lisa and Eb tour the White House, and Mr. Kimball makes official trouble.

When a charmingly sweet doe wanders onto the Douglas farm, an enchanted Lisa befriends the beautiful animal. Having had her heart won over, Lisa resolves to have all deer hunting banned in Hooterville, winning support however necessary.

Farmhand Eb plans to take his girlfriend to a fancy restaurant for her birthday. Only problem is he can't afford it. Oliver encourages Eb to get creative and figure out how to earn the money himself. And if Eb is anything, it's creative.
A sinister town boss called Pat Barnes has exploited almost everyone in the town.
The adopted son of a preacher comes upon a village that is under the thumb of a deranged ex-Confederate officer, who is - among other things - stealing land from the locals with phony land grants.

During the Civil War, three outlaws face execution for selling guns to the enemy — until a Confederate general spares them. Their mission: recover a hidden fortune in gold under the watch of an officer. But rival treasure hunters turn their path to freedom into a deadly race.

A relentless bounty hunter pursues a brutal gang of gunrunners deep into Mexico. As he crosses the lawless borderlands, he’s drawn into a deadly chase where justice and vengeance blur in the desert heat.

When bandits begin kidnapping Clayton City’s elite for ransom, Sartana is called in to restore order. But the gang’s mysterious leader sees him as a deadly threat and hires four expert killers to take him down. To save the town and expose the mastermind, Sartana must survive every trap and betrayal.
Several competing groups and mavericks (including the lead character Cuchillo) are hunting a gold treasure of $3,000,000. The gold was reserved for the Mexican revolution.

Everyone wants to know who the Mexican is. He always answer slowly, "my name is Pecos". Pecos Martinez to be exact, and he's returned to his hometown of Houston to settle up with Clain, the leader of a gang of cut-throats. Clain is busy looking for the money from a recent robbery that's been stolen from him. Soon the stolen cash in Pecos' vengeance entwine and all hell breaks loose. Behind the scenes a Bible touting Undertaker (Umberto Raho), a cowardly saloon owner, & a helpful saloon girl beco
Robber Roy King loses his wife, Alicia, to revolutionary Montero. Despite their rivalry they collaborate in an attempt to rob the Mexican government of one million dollars.

programmes.t: The White, the Yellow and the Black
programmes.d: In the 19th century, when the Japanese Emperor sends a gift pony to the US President it gets stolen and ransomed by Indians but Sheriff Gideon aided by an inept Japanese servant offers to deliver the ransom.

In San Felipe, bandits target gold meant for the railroad - until a decoy chest thwarts them. When newcomers arrive, a masked gunman begins sabotaging the outlaws. But the real mastermind may be the town’s respected leader, hiding treachery behind wealth and charm.

Bounty hunter Stan Ross arrives in Canyon City, drawn by a bank robbery. Hired by the town’s powerful banker Jefferson, he hunts down a gang of Mexican bandits - only to uncover shocking secrets. As Ross digs deeper, he realizes Jefferson’s grip on the town is far more dangerous than he thought.

programmes.t: May God Forgive You... But I Won't
programmes.d: While Cjamango is away from his ranch six bandits attack and kill all the members of his family.
A frontier family crosses the U.S. by wagon train, hoping for a better life in the Oregon Territory.

The eldest daughter of a pioneer family is kidnapped by a mysterious Indian tribe and the eldest son pursues. In order to win back his sister's freedom, he must sacrifice his own life by passing the test of "Crooked Sky" and shield his sister from an executioner's arrow. Along the way, he recruits a broken down, drunk prospector to help him track down the unknown tribe and rescue his sister.

As settlers encroach on Native lands, the Assiniboins go to war while Apache chief Winnetou tries to maintain peace. A corrupt oilman, Bud Forrester, orchestrates attacks to provoke conflict and seize oil-rich territory. Old Shatterhand, Winnetou, and Lord Castlepool unite to expose the scheme and prevent a full-scale war.
A Texas sheriff and his younger brother travel across the Mexican border to confront the man who killed their father.

Outlaws attack a band of settlers and kill everyone except a pregnant woman who's rescued by a band of Indians. The woman dies giving birth but Chief White Bear adopts her male baby, naming him "Shining Sky," and raising him as brother to his own son, Black Wolf.

programmes.t: If you meet Sartana... Pray for your Death
programmes.d: Crooked bankers plan an insurance swindle and hire a Mexican gang to steal the bank's gold but they also pay Lasky's gang to kill the Mexicans.
A mysterious woman persuades two cowboys to help her in a revenge scheme.

Sabata and Mangosta are bank robbers, who after a bank job, through a series of events, end up teaming up with the bank clerk, Peter. They then go on the run with Peter's boss and a hired posse equipped with the latest technology in weapons on their trail.

In the final months of the Civil War, Joe’s brother is unjustly slain by a Northern captain. Consumed by grief and fury, Joe joins a band of Southern fighters who refuse to surrender, seeking justice and redemption amid the dying embers of war.

Johnny MaGee arrives in a mining town and clashes with banker Anthony Burton, who uses underhanded tactics to acquire gold mines. As Burton manipulates the locals, including offering to wipe out a doctor’s debts in exchange for his sister’s marriage, Johnny finds an ally in bounty hunter Ted. But Burton’s reach goes far beyond the mines.

A major robbery spirals out of control when two young men cross paths with ruthless Mexican bandits and a corrupt businessman—both desperate to reclaim the stolen loot. Caught in a deadly chase, the youths face danger, betrayal, and the fight for survival.

programmes.t: Dig Your Grave Friend... Sabata's Coming
programmes.d: Steve McGowan returns from war to avenge his father’s murder by a ruthless landowner. Imprisoned, he escapes with a bandit and steals a stagecoach—only to find the villain’s fiancée inside. As hired guns close in, alliances shift, and the fight for justice takes an unexpected turn.

Romeo & Angela talk for the first time in years, but can their relationship be healed? Sam & Egypt celebrate their second wedding ceremony. To celebrate 50 years of Hip Hop, legends grace the stage, along with the cast, in an epic performance.

Bow Wow's arrest blows up in the tabloids and causes an uproar with Da Brat. R. Kelly's arrest ignites a buzzing child support battle with ex-wife Drea Kelly. Waka Flocka and wife Tammy Rivera put their wedding renewal vows to the ultimate test.

Bow faces tough love about his arrest and a dark cloud threatens to send him back to jail. Tammy's heart-to-heart with Drea Kelly sparks a revelation about her marriage to Waka. Deb's godson Brandon returns but bad blood isn't reconciled so easily.

A surprise visit from Angela Simmons rocks Bow's world! Tammy's insecurities threaten her first sexy music video. Ayana and Brandon face off and Waka questions Brandon's motives. Eazy-E's daughter seeks guidance from Deb and Brat.

Breaking news regarding R. Kelly's child support battle explodes into chaos. Deb and Brat clash over Drea Kelly. Ayana raises suspicions about Brandon firefighting; Bow and Brandon face off. ReeMarkable's performance backfires.

JD's throws a star-studded skate party including Usher and T-Boz. Snoop dishes out tough love on Bow. Brat blows up on LisaRaye when bankruptcy pushes her to a breaking point. Waka warns Deb that Brandon needs to steer clear of the family or else.

Bow enters dangerous territory when he meets a fiery new woman. ReeMarkable blows off her boyfriend and suffers the pay back. Deb has a family dinner to confront Brandon about a big fat lie. Waka reaches his boiling point and goes in for the kill.

Brandon's lies are exposed and that brings Brandon and Waka nearly to blows. Warning signs arise when Corri marks her territory with Bow. Brat questions ReeMarkable's intentions. Bow disses Drea Kelly right to her face.
Tammy goes ballistic when she catches Waka in a lie. Bow is blindsided when he learns of Corri's dangerous past. ReeMarkable disrespects Deb and Da Brat and battle lines are drawn.

After putting Corri on ice, Bow makes a bold move and invites his ex, Angela Simmons to Shaniah's 21st birthday bash. Corri keeps tabs on Bow's moves. Tension between Da Brat and Drea Kelly escalates. Waka enters the lion's den with Tammy.

Brandon returns and makes a shocking confession. Deb and Brat explode after giving ReeMarkable one last chance. All hell breaks loose when Corri shows up on a rampage against Bow. Tammy's big NYC show goes off the rails.

As Atlanta emerges from quarantine, the cast struggles to navigate a new world in troubling times. Bow's scandalous album rocks Atlanta, Ayana receives a terrifying health diagnosis, and Deb drops a bomb that shocks Waka and threatens her reputation.

Despite warnings, Bow threatens to tell all about his exes on his new album. When an ex shows up in ATL, Bow is forced to face the past. Deb's secret creates turmoil that could tank her reputation. The stress of it sends someone over the edge.

Tammy and Deb clash over politics; Waka gets caught in the crossfire. Pimpin' has to face the music when his ex Diamond confronts him. Sexual tension fuels their fiery fight suggesting they may not be over after all. Jhonni has to fess up to Deb.

Brat presses Judy to move to ATL. Hurricane's desperate to help a sick Ayana, but Shaniah takes a different approach. Ree's ready to reconcile with Brat and Deb, but will they give her another chance? Diamond's album release party ends in turmoil.

A fight at Diamond's party steals her spotlight, creating a conflict that threatens to tear the cast apart when Deb unites everyone on a new project. Brat is angry when she hears that Deb is keeping things from her. Ayana recovers from COVID-19.

Bow and Brat refuse to be part of Deb's project, causing a huge rift that may be permanent. Turning to Waka for help, Deb might not like the tough love he gives. Ree wants to make things right with Ayana over an ugly Twitter feud, but Ayana refuses.

Brat appeals to JD about Bow's scandalous new album, but his response throws her for a loop. Shaniah and JD join forces to make positive changes in their community. BT's birthday party culminates in an all-out girl fight.

Jesseca persuades Brat to give Jhonni another chance, but tempers flare when Brat and Jhonni face off. Bow learns that one wild night could affect the rest of his life. Tammy's shocked when Ayana and Ree's longstanding feud spirals out of control.

Pimpin' and Diamond call it quits, and Khi can't resist making a move when he learns Diamond is single. Meanwhile, Bow anxiously awaits the results of his paternity test and considers how a baby son could impact his future.

Bow finds out if he's a new daddy. An emergency at Deb and Brat's EP party causes Jhonni to suffer a cataclysmic meltdown, and Waka is caught in the crossfire. Meanwhile, Diamond embraces newly single life, and Khi prepares to make his move.

Angela opens up about her devastating breakup and the pressures of living in the spotlight. Vanessa throws a party to reunite the heirs and clear the air while Romeo gets caught up in a love triangle. Boogie's addiction takes a turn for the worst.

Tee Tee and Briana beef over Romeo's affections. Dame enlists Master P to scare Boogie straight. Angela moves to LA for a fresh start. Romeo hopes to get close to his newly-single former flame. Red flags are raised about naive Egypt's relationship.

Game night at Pepa's house spirals into fight night! Dame and Pep clash over the severity of Boogie's addiction while Briana enters to confront a nasty rumor. Angela and Romeo reunite for the first time since Angela's breakup.

Angela and Romeo's Orlando getaway leads to a hotel nightcap. Briana and Pepa clash at a releasing ceremony when Pepa brings alcoholic spirits. Boogie is blindsided when he is lead to a surprise drug intervention.

Boogie's intervention spirals out of control when Kristinia and Briana nearly come to blows! Romeo and Angela discuss their relationship. Angela drops a bomb on her and Vanessa's business plan. On the brink of destruction, Boogie checks into rehab.

Pepa's son Tyran comes to town with old baggage in tow. Tyran interrogates Egypt's boyfriend Sam. Drama ensues at a welcome party for Tyran. Master P is blindsided when he discovers that his incarcerated brother has gone on a hunger strike!

The danger surrounding Master P's incarcerated brother comes to a head. Tee Tee plays cupid for Briana to make amends, but her grand plan backfires! Tyran struggles to get Pepa's attention. After a blowup, Angela and Vanessa must unite for charity.

Boogie is released from rehab and temptation strikes! Master P mentors the guys on a camping trip. Family therapy with Pepa and her son, Tyran, bursts into flames. Kristinia meets her cousin Kyndall, El DeBarge's daughter, for the first time ever.

Angela and her siblings talk about marriage while Tee Tee goes on a first date with Romeo. Tee Tee's hair event sparks trouble when Kristinia's cousin, Kyndall, and her enemy, Briana, face off. Since their fight night blowup, Pepa and Dame reunite!

Marriage is on the radar! JoJo is pressed to make a proposal. Meanwhile, Romeo's torn between Angela and Tee Tee. Egypt's bikini shoot turns left when her boyfriend, Sam tries to take over. Drama ignites when momager, Pepa, checks Egypt!

Kristinia moves to Sin City and throws a welcome party! The rivalry between Briana and Kristinia comes to a head. Tee Tee is blindsided when Romeo reveals that he has a secret crush on another woman! Panic strikes when Egypt and Sam run off to elope!

Angela is shell-shocked when she suffers a major loss. Romeo runs to Angela's side. Boogie betrays his family to avoid his father, Dame. A family dispute between the Pepas comes to a head at Romeo's yacht party. A table is flipped and fists fly!

Angela is blindsided when Vanessa takes business matters into her own hands. Pepa's security guard turned boyfriend violates his new father figure role. A disgruntled Briana comes for Tee Tee. In a long-awaited reunion, Dame unleashes on Boogie!

Boogie and Dame have a life-altering meet up. Sparks fly between Romeo and Angela. Angela avoids Vanessa at the racetrack and pushes Vanessa to her breaking point. A shocking scandal rocks Pepa's world when Aundre's past comes back to haunt him.

Lil Twist brings trouble to Dame's Culture Vulture Event which threatens Sam. Meanwhile, Twist has eyes for Egypt. Romeo stands up to Master P and suffers the blowback. A scandal from Aundre's past emerges and jeopardizes Pepa's million-dollar deal.

Romeo and Bow Wow face off in an epic battle of the Lil's! Pepa's conflicted between her career and her relationship. On a romantic stroll in New Orleans, Angela and Romeo take shocking next steps to move forward in their relationship.

Angela and Romeo's double date backfires! Pepa's relationship with Aundre takes a turn for the worst. Tee Tee throws a singles party where an uninvited guest pops up with a vengeance. Sam and Lil Twist nearly come to blows over Egypt.

Romeo finds himself in troubled waters with Angela when he drops out of their double date. Dame confronts his nemesis. Pepa struggles with a broken heart. Master P warns Eric about digging up Eazy-E's death. Vanessa's birthday surprise.

Angela opens up about her past at a Fearless Conference. Dame and Rocky struggle to conceive. Vanessa exposes a shocking secret. Suspicions around Eazy-E's death deepen. Briana blows up and storms off when feelings about her father are triggered.

Angela is set up on a hot date with someone other than Romeo. Meanwhile, JoJo prepares a surprise of a lifetime. Drama ignites at Lil Twist's listening party when Briana spirals down a dangerous path and everyone is shook.

Vanessa confronts Romeo about his feelings for Angela. Briana's birthday goes up in flames when Briana and Eric nearly come to blows. JoJo surprises his sisters when he takes them shopping for an engagement ring.

After a blind date disaster, Angela is blindsided when Romeo surprises her in New York. JoJo panics to pull off a marriage proposal. In the aftermath of an explosive birthday brawl, Briana's invite to Boogie's important showcase has everyone on edge.
Just when Angela and Romeo take a chance at love, Angela's world falls apart when tragedy strikes and shocks all. Dame checks on a troubled Briana who makes a brutal decision no one saw coming.
Romeo drops a bombshell on the Simmons family that rocks Angela to her core! Meanwhile, Egypt's boyfriend Sam does sneaky business at a pawn shop. Panic strikes when a secret engagement is exposed.

Angela and Romeo's rivalry comes to a head and sends shockwaves through Romeo's party. Vanessa's stuck in the middle and JoJo flies off the handle! Meanwhile, a scandal strikes Salt-N-Pepa. Angela is blindsided when Briana does the unexpected.

Romeo blocks everyone on social media and causes uproar, but Angela has receipts! Tee Tee and Tyran join forces to derail Sam and Egypt's trip to the altar, and warn Pepa and Treach before it's too late. Angela plans to squash the beef with Briana.

JoJo seeks marriage guidance from Rev Run when JoJo's baby fever strikes a bad chord with Tanice. Pepa warns Tee Tee to stop meddling in Egypt and Sam's relationship while Briana rages on. Ava breaks down over the legal war with her father Dame.

Encuentro en la estación: Anna Arkadievna Karenina, esposa de un alto funcionario del gobierno, llega a Moscú para ayudar a su hermano Stiva en una difícil situación familiar. En la estación de tren, conoce por casualidad al joven y distinguido oficial Alexéi Alexandrovich Vronski…

Las carreras de oficiales: Karenina y Vronski se reencuentran durante una competencia ecuestre. Un desafortunado error de Vronski provoca la caída y muerte de su caballo. Profundamente afectada por la escena, Anna pierde el conocimiento y, en su angustia, le confiesa todo a su esposo…
La boda: El terrateniente Levin le propone matrimonio por segunda vez a Kiti Shcherbátskaya, y en esta ocasión, ella acepta…
Esa no soy yo: Anna da a luz a una niña. Dos pensamientos la atormentan: la culpa hacia su esposo y el miedo a la muerte durante el parto. Finalmente, consigue que su marido perdone a Vronski…

Justicia divina: Vronski, desesperado por encontrar una solución a su situación insostenible, viaja a visitar a su madre en busca de dinero. Anna interpreta su partida como la peor traición a su amor…

Frank Sinatra's barkeep father and midwife mother had loose affiliations with organized crime that assisted Frank in his rise to stardom; John F Kennedy's father's bootlegging past cultivated criminal connections that helped him to run for President.

Kennedy wins the Presidency; Robert Kennedy, hellbent on cracking down on the Mafia, was appointed Attorney General; Hoover discovers a love triangle, he tells the President to cut all ties with the Mafia, including Sinatra.

Small-town tailor AJ Pratt catches the attention of the Kansas City Mob; they move him to Las Vegas, where he's plugged into the star-studded scene designing for celebrities, politicians, and mobsters; he learns a valuable lesson about respect.

AJ gains a new client: Pablo Escobar, and Escobar introduces AJ to the world of cocaine; when the FBI cracks down on the mob, AJ steps in to help broker a deal, winning favor with the mob while expanding his cocaine smuggling empire.
AJ struggles to balance his fashion empire, mafia ties and cocaine cartel when the police come knocking.

AJ's empire comes crashing down as the FBI closes in, mob violence spirals out of control, and AJ's closest ally is murdered; after barely surviving an attempt on his life, AJ flees the state and claims to turn over a new leaf.
After shooting the man who murdered his wife, a Danish settler (Mads Mikkelsen) incurs the wrath of the man's brother (Jeffrey Dean Morgan), a ruthless land baron who rules their frontier town.

In 1977, the young scion of a family real estate empire buys the NFL's San Francisco 49ers; his efforts to build a winner fail until he hires an outcast coach with radical ideas; together they construct a team that begins to challenge NFL royalty.

In 1981, the 49ers complete their miracle Super Bowl run, galvanizing the troubled, iconoclastic city of San Francisco; as the 80s wear on, they celebrate another Super Bowl, welcome new superstar players, and weather drama off the field.

Just as the 49ers appear to reach their peak in the late 1980s, a shocking playoff loss and the burgeoning quarterback controversy between superstar Joe Montana and the up-and-coming Steve Young threaten to tear the team apart.

Written off by the football world, the 1988 49ers come together for another miracle run; Super Bowl XXIII will make or break the team's dynasty, and it might be the last game for the team's brilliant but exhausted head coach, Bill Walsh.

programmes.t: Wasp Woman: Murder of a B Movie Queen
programmes.d: In 1986, cult actress Susan Cabot is found dead in her Los Angeles home; suspicion immediately falls on her son, Timothy Roman, the only witness and immediate suspect; what begins as a shocking Hollywood murder soon opens into a darker story.

programmes.t: Wasp Woman: Murder of a B Movie Queen
programmes.d: The investigation deepens and Timothy's story becomes more complex; Timothy's life was shaped not only by his mother's troubled past but by a chapter in American medical history, as a patient enrolled in a now-buried clinical experiment.

programmes.t: Wasp Woman: Murder of a B Movie Queen
programmes.d: Susan's body is discovered in her bedroom, bloodied, broken and surrounded by confusion; Timothy offers a surreal account of masked intruders, but his story unravels quickly; under pressure, he admits the truth.
Among the secret murders explored are Judith Roberts, Mary Judge in Leeds in 1968, a schoolgirl killed in Staffordshire in 1972 and Carol Wilkinson, a bakery worker murdered in Bradford in 1977.

The pressure continues to build on West Yorkshire Police; on top of the crimes that police decide to include in the Ripper investigation, murders and attempted murders with a clear link to the killer are discarded and left unsolved.

programmes.t: True Crime Story: It Couldn't Happen Here

programmes.t: True Crime Story: It Couldn't Happen Here

programmes.t: True Crime Story: It Couldn't Happen Here

programmes.t: True Crime Story: It Couldn't Happen Here
programmes.d: Years after the body of a young woman is found strangled to death in a creek bed, law enforcement finally closes the case; a closer look raises questions about the investigation.

programmes.t: True Crime Story: It Couldn't Happen Here

It was a mystery that plagued law enforcement for over years: four unidentified bodies found inside barrels in the woods; one woman searching for answers from her own troubled past sets herself on a journey to give the victims back their names.

A young man whose childhood was marked by tragedy learns of a relatively unknown serial killer, and finds himself thinking about unidentified victims; it isn't long before that pursuit becomes a full-time job and identifying victims an obsession.

A woman regrets lending electronic devices to her niece.
Repayment of a loan; damages to a family truck.
A crash into a parked classic car; tenants feud.
A cosmetic company owner accuses a boutique of throwing out an expensive display.
Repairman has not returned a truck; children are accused of throwing rocks at a family's cars.
Roommates fall out over the pet policy; a former tenant wants her deposit back.
A car crashes into a home and a parked vehicle.
Disagreements escalate to physical fights and threats of witchcraft.
Ex-lovers argue over ownership of mutual possessions; a woman says she was sold fake hair.
Truck used as collateral; liability for a fender-bender.
Payment for child care; pet fish die.
A good Samaritan's roommate fails to pay even his small portion.
A homeowner says a handyman never finished a job; back rent and a security deposit.
An unfair vehicle trade; vermin in a rental home.
A store awning of bad quality.
A mechanic fails to fix a car; a missing tool set.
A woman says her co-worker slapped her at work; comics feud over breaking a lease.
Injuries from a dog bite; a parrot breeder wants a bird returned.
A family friend makes a leak worse and refuses to return payment.
A dispute over the quality of a vehicle listed online has strangers arguing over who should keep it.
Back rent; ownership of a car.
Businesswomen sue for their intellectual property after editor uses their essays without permission.
A stolen lockbox with a handgun in it; an injured dog.
Was a woman taken for a ride in motorcycle sale?; woman fired after two weeks on the job sues her ex-boss for expenses.
Woman claims her ex wasn't a business partner, he was just a mooch; slurs scratched on a car.
Woman claims she paid for her ex-fiancée's dental work, and she wants the money back; couple claims their wedding photographer was not a "professional"?
Building manager claims the tenant broke her lease and took everything; tenant alleges that he sexually harassed her before leaving.
Breast implants.
Woman sues her ex for damage he caused while allegedly stalking her; ex-lovers feud over a rent-to-own refrigerator.
Good Samaritan hit by bucket.
Mom wants to teach her son a lesson; did vacation photos end a friendship?
Woman sued by ex who allegedly won't leave her alone; gambling debt or loan from a friend?
Who gets the engagement ring?; woman's terrier is missing a toe!
Feuding sisters end up in Judy's court over a credit card bill; aunt sues her niece over a real estate deal gone bad.
Ex-con sues ex-girlfriend; woman wants former son-in-law to pay up.
Couple in court after "ugly" divorce; taken for a ride during whirlwind romance?
Speed racer gets bopped in the nose; man drives car through laundromat.
Leather jacket lost in the coat check; manager sues producer over music money.
Blood test reveals baby wasn't his!; a family affair?
Tow truck driver claims BMW owner attacked him; man sues his ex for custody of their cocker spaniel.
Heartbroken sitter wants back pay for helping raise baby.
Damaged property; broken contract.
Ex-wife vs. the other woman; man sues over pricey vacuum cleaner.
Dad sues for family jewels; woman wants tax money back from her ex.
Mom sues ex for taking away daughter's car; man sues brother for giving him a massage.
Rock n' roller sues 79-year-old landlord; woman claims magician levitated her, then dropped her!
Officer sues over post-accident bite; did man crash car on a beer run?
Salesman says woman owes him for a bag of beauty products; she claims he's a con artist; on and off couple in court over car.
Did grandparents kidnap granddaughters?; the grandparents deny the accusation and claim they received bad legal advice.
Elaborate wedding dress rips friendship apart; friend hot under the collar over unpaid loan.
Man left for new life, but got a new wife!; man says brother's interest on loan is criminal.
Psychic hotline phone bill battle; Vegas loan paid with a bad check?
Fighting over child custody; Judge Judy orders former friends to get coffee.
Man thinks he overpaid child support; did mom give money or was it a loan?
Mom wants custody of son back from her parents.
Babysitter chaos in the courtroom; boy shaves his eyebrows at the babysitter's.
Child support dispute.
Mom claims daughter stole her belongings; exes face off over tires and computers.
BMW broke down in the car wash; ex-lovers argue over checking account money.
Man sues his ex-wife's new boyfriend.
Did "Captain Good" do a bad thing?
Exes clash in court over bounced checks.
Designated driver gets stuck with ticket; band members clash over a woman.
Woman can't collect on collect calls; performers are peeved over canceled event.
Bitter exes clash over engagement ring and other expenses.
Will recordings prove Yogi's rental story?
Is serial dater a serial borrower; a romantic cruise that never was.
Couple claims their neighbor egged their house.
Cousins argue over crashed Caddy; bouncer claims he was bonked with a high-heeled shoe.
Did woman's ex take back her engagement ring?
A stamp collection and a married man; personal ad romance ends in court.
Whose toaster is it?
Comedian's stand-up gig gets canceled, but he wants to be paid; engagement called off.
Who should pay for daughter's braces?
Man is caught between girlfriend and ex; Halloween horseplay ends in broken nose.
Illusionist claims pet store sold her lizards without her knowing; estranged daughter wants Grandma's ring.
Roommates face off over a bird, a dog and puppies.
White wedding turns red; man gets booted from salsa club.
Exes battle over Easter Sunday fight.
Mom sues estranged daughter.
Man denies burning ex's truck; man wants his dream vacation.
Man accused of putting cat litter in ex's engine.
Man starts dating friend's ex; man wants his watch back.
Neighbor calls cops on noisy kids.
Too many sleepovers caused man to move; teen wants used car deposit back.
A marriage gone bad and a computer gone missing.
Couple ends engagement at friend's wedding.
Man denies breaking woman's ribs during a hug; man claims former fiancée and her mom are suing him because he left her for a dancer.
Man denies using church friend for money.
Man sues international bride for calling the cops.
Woman wants her stereo back; divorced couple fights over minivan.
Judge Judy schools "disrespectful" defendant.
Sports hat "hustle" goes wrong; now, who pays?
Teenage joyride ends in tragedy; man denies scamming woman out of paycheck.
Bride called off the wedding -- groom kept the cash; woman claims her ex-roommate's boyfriend ran up an enormous phone bill and refuses to pay it back.
Two corrections officers' post-break up battle; tenant denies frequent guests and unpaid rent.
Man says woman reporting a gun cost him his job.
Dad says son won't move out and wants back rent.
Renters claim they're traumatized by "illegal" entry; woman denies stealing singles magazine client list.
Woman wants custody of exotic plants; was loaning money a mutual thing?
Man denies swindling woman; loan or gift? Woman wants her silverware back.
Former friends feud; woman wants her late husband's tools back.

Her Honor presides over two cases in this episode. In the first, a woman is accused of repeatedly backing into a teen's car in her own driveway; her daughter testifies against her. In the 2nd case, a man alleges that at the sight of two growling pit bulls on his front porch, he retreated to the safety of his new car. He says the dogs proceeded to bite and scratch his week-old, luxury vehicle.
A tenant's violation of pool rules leads a property manager to take drastic action. The tenant then sues for an alleged assault, attorney fees and emotional distress.
After the bars close, drinking continues in a park but ends when a flying beer can causes thousands in dental damages to a partygoer. Former high school teammates fight over who is to blame.

In this episode, the Judge rules on two cases. Up first, the Judge shares memories of her own childhood dance experience while mediating a payment dispute between a dance studio owner and a single mother. In the second case, a woman says her roommate's boyfriend entered their shared apartment unannounced and with his own key. She claims the voicing of her safety concerns led to her eviction.
A woman claims her former employer accused her of being a drug addict and withheld wages. Her employer countersues for defamation of character.
A failed attempt at living together leaves sisters in a bitter dispute over alleged child neglect, a mysterious call to CPS and police intervention after a lockout.

Her Honor presides over two cases in this episode. In the first case, a Father's Day standoff between a teenager and his girlfriends' stepsister ends with the violent smashing of a car mirror. In the second, a man admits that he was only present during the euthanization of a beloved pet because his ex-girlfriend said she would forgive a debt if he provided emotional support.
A spa owner sues a former employee for the 10k court maximum claiming that the aesthetician broke their non-compete agreement and started working well within the seven-mile radius of her business.

Despite being slapped with a restraining order for threatening his ex son-in-law, a grandfather continues to seek payback from him. An eviction, marital debt and care for his grandchildren come into play.

In this episode, the Judge rules on two cases. Up first, a high school teacher accuses a student of a hit-and-run; the teen's father is reprimanded for allowing his uninsured teen to drive without a license. In the second case, after a woman's business is shut down by the government due to Covid, ex-roommates accuse each other of taking advantage of the rental relief program.
A landlord's new property comes complete with previous tenants who sue him for child endangerment due to alleged lead poisoning. The landlord countersues when they stop paying rent.

Her Honor presides over two cases in this episode. In the first case, a hair-salon owner helps a friend pay for a luxury vehicle which he proceeds to crash; instead of paying her back, he then buys an expensive electric sports car. In the second case, A man accuses his ex-friend of repossessing his car without just cause and demands payback for the 5K he put into it.
An unlicensed contractor sues for damages after a married couple stops payment on a $4200 check for demolition work. They accuse him of property theft and dispute payment for a tractor rental.

A man accuses his sister of kidnapping his special-needs teenager who was, unbeknownst to him, in need of life-saving, emergency brain surgery. The sister is seeking reimbursement for costs associated with that surgery and return of her nephew’s property.

In this episode, the Judge rules on two cases. Up first, years after the death of their mother, sisters fight over the disbursement details of her personal belongings. A woman says she only wants one photo with her mother as a keepsake. In the second case, an independent contractor on disability sues an old friend for an unpaid loan and money allegedly stolen from their joint bank account.

Police body-cam footage captures a woman's admission and regret that her pit bull attacked a neighbor's miniature schnauzer. Her actions after the attack tell a different story when pictures surface that show her off-leash pit bull roaming the neighborhood.
An amateur pilot sues for the 10K court maximum when his plane is allegedly damaged by a certified flight instructor who hit an object on the runway. Damning video evidence comes into play.

programmes.t: One-Wheel Whammy and All Bets Are Off
programmes.d: In this episode, the Judge rules on two cases. Up first, a teenager on a one-wheel, electric skateboard plows into the side of a car, flies onto the hood and falls to the ground. Lucky to be alive, he now faces a motorist suing for vehicle damages. In the next case, a single father wins a $36,000 sports gambling payout and gives his ex-roommate 6K to 'hold' for him. She claims it was a gift.

Both parties seek the 10K court maximum when a man's death brings to light the fact that he was never married to his 'wife'. Family members and his estranged 'partner' fight over an allegedly false police report and personal property.

A woman is lured into an ill-conceived 'intervention' at a friend's home by being told she will receive drugs once she gets there. She is sued for breaking a TV in a fit of rage, but countersues for damages caused by the emotional trauma she suffered.

Scrappy the French Bulldog makes an appearance in court when a woman sues her kickboxer exboyfriend for custody of their shared pet. The Judge admonishes them for making a long-term pet decision in a short-term relationship.

Her Honor presides over two cases in this episode. In the first case, when a plumber sues an employer for filing an allegedly false restraining order, the Judge must decide if an ominous voicemail was cause enough for the complaint. In the second case, long after a relationship ends, dueling text messages help the Judge decipher the facts about a disputed loan between ex-lovers.

In this two-part episode, a man fears for his safety and leaves his home when six men show up to defend his roommate during a heated argument. He returns the next day to find his room has been thoroughly vandalized.
In part two, a woman claims she was framed for vandalism and falsely arrested. She seeks compensation for slashed tires and alleged cyberbullying.
When divorced parents sue each other for the 10k court maximum, a teenager is caught in the middle of a feud over a 'maliciously' towed vehicle and multiple reports to child services.

In this episode, the Judge rules on two cases. Up first, a man with 4 children by 3 different women is at the center of a fight between two of the mothers. He remains silent while they fight over harassment, alleged gun-brandishing and vandalism. In the 2nd case, a bride only offers $50 to her planner who paid thousands to help make sure her California ranch wedding took place during the pandemic.
A fight breaks out between female veterinary workers and a passionate pet owner in seek of emergency care for his injured cat. He sues for damages after receiving a black eye in the parking lot.
A woman's demand that her 4K security deposit be returned is marred by the fact that she took the doorbell with her when she left.
In this two-part episode, a cosmetics salesman is accused of accosting and holding a woman captive for hours plying her with compliments and free samples.
In part two, the customer 'escapes' by purchasing an $8,000 rejuvenation wand and sues for fraud soon after.

After 'kidnapping' her own child from a family member and evading police, a woman is charged with child endangerment and spends four months in jail. She accuses her mother of stealing thousands from her while she was imprisoned.

The Judge rules on two cases in this episode. In the first case, a woman loans 10K to a new friend to support his supplement business; he claims it was an investment in a plan to sell 'happy pills' at festivals. Up next, a single mother with four children and good credit sues for 10k when her stepfather reneges on a car deal. She is left with payments for 2 vehicles and a dwindling credit score.
Six years of peace and harmony between divorcees come to an abrupt halt when three ATVs and a $58,000 truck are at stake.

When a young man is caught cheating three times, he is expelled from school. His steadfast father reverses charges for his son's tuition and is now faced with a lawsuit by administration for doing so.
When neighbors feud over property and attorney fees, the Judge shares her own personal story about a neighbor who refused to amicably resolve an easement issue.

The Judge rules on two cases in this episode. In the first, an online influencer seeks the 10K court maximum from a tailor he claims botched the creation of his dream costume. The 'ill-fitting' ensemble is modelled in court by its disgruntled owner. Up next, a caregiver takes $400 from a 90-year-old dementia patient because 'she told me to.' After her patient suffers a fall, she is dismissed.
To avoid points on his driving record, a trucker offers cash to a fellow motorist after an accident. Their arrangement falls apart when repair estimate amounts and dates vary wildly.

Her Honor presides over two cases in this episode. In the first case, a woman makes a deposit on a foal six months before its birth but wants out of the contract once the animal is born. Believing the baby horse could not be insured, she sues for breach of contract. In the second case, a disabled veteran sues for a $6500 refund when the paint job on her beloved 1969 VW Volkswagen starts 'bubbling'.
A man is sued for property damage to a $1400 a month pool house with no indoor plumbing. He claims his landlord assaulted him in a fight over unpaid utilities and disrespect.

In this episode, the Judge rules on two cases. Up first, after a popular medical student tragically drowns, his friends raise over 40K in his honor. His mother and sister fight over his property and the funds collected. Next, a woman denies being under the influence of anything other than Benadryl when she slams into a parked car and pushes it 25 feet down a sidewalk. She is sued for damages.
An ex-con's fresh start with his wife in a new home is marred by their landlords' lawsuit over property damage, unpaid rent and defamation. A missing claw-foot tub comes into play.

In this episode, the Judge rules on two cases. Up first, a mother and son are no longer on speaking terms after a deal to purchase a van falls apart. He claims the inoperable van was a gift and that any discussion of money was only to appease her after the fact. In the next case, a mechanical engineer and a programmer fight over profits from their shared cryptocurrency mining business.
A not-so-neighborly dog walk results in vandalism and police intervention. A woman sues for a false arrest, lawyer fees and damages caused by the trauma of a night in jail.

In this episode, the Judge rules on two cases. Up first, a man changes his story many times when asked to prove that monies loaned to him by an ex were never meant to be paid back. In the next case, following their break-up, a man loans the mother of his child 10K to escape the burden of 500-800% interest rates on her personal debt. They fight over payback when a new boyfriend comes into play.

Both parties seek the 10K court maximum when a real-estate purchase 10 miles south of the border goes awry. A new homeowner is accused of illegally evicting the previous owner and extorting her for money by holding her pets as ransom.

Her Honor presides over two cases in this episode. In the first case, a victim of a hit-and-run makes the split-second decision to slam her car into a house instead of oncoming traffic. Her actions may have saved lives, but she is sued for property damage by a homeowner. Up next, an alcohol-fueled altercation over a cheating girlfriend leaves friends at odds over an alleged assault and two kayaks.
Two large dogs set their sights on a 38-foot, inflatable, obstacle course and chew into a portion of the structure. Business partners seek compensation for damages to their party rental equipment.

Her Honor presides over two cases in this episode. In the first case, a 21-year-old drives her guardian's car without permission, crashes and totals the vehicle leaving family members to fight over damages. Up next, former gambling buddies fight over a jackpot win, missing jewelry and a little white lie to a boyfriend about where the grocery money went.

The Judge rules on two cases in this episode. In the first, both parties seek the 10K court maximum when old friends fight over an RV escalates into a physical assault. Up next, new parents hire an event planner to organize a Sip n' See celebration of their newborn child. The planner backs out when jealousy and threats surface; she is sued for a refund.

Bad blood between unwed parents leads to a fight over a three-year-old car accident and an attempt to collect far more than the car is worth. Jail time, alleged domestic violence and admitted drug use come into play.
In a small Idaho farming community, a teenager sells four piglets to a neighbor and expects to be paid in full. The buyer claims all four animals died and that he owes nothing.

An unlikely friendship develops between a male nurse and a female inmate through a prison pen pal program. Soon after her release, their once-supportive relationship devolves into a fight over stimulus checks and a car loan.

The Judge rules on two cases in this episode. First, despite eye-witness testimony, a man insists that his unlicensed girlfriend was not driving his truck when it backed into a neighbor's house. His teenage son backs up his story. Next, a mechanic refuses to return a woman's wrecked car until he is paid; she admits to spending insurance money intended for car repairs on her own personal expenses.
A senior victim of bank fraud seeks restitution from her teenage, great granddaughter who made the mistake of accepting mysterious checks from an ex-con relative.
Teenagers who met in foster care get into a catfight over a boy. Their fight escalates into an aggressive act of caught-on-tape vandalism, an arrest and a 10K lawsuit.

Her Honor presides over two cases in this episode. First, a young woman breaks up with her live-in boyfriend and starts to date their new roommate. The ex-boyfriend sues the happy new couple for $10K and for the return of his two cats. Next, business partners pay $6K to rent a party space for teens; they sue for breach of contract when event restrictions are put in place without their approval.

A man is sued for alleged failure to pay his late mother's caregiver. He accuses the healthcare worker of contributing to the 'delinquency of an elderly patient' by giving his dying mother cigarettes and marijuana.

A 14-year-old girl steals her mother's car, goes on a joyride and T-bones an unsuspecting motorist on her way to work. The teenager runs from the crash site; the injured motorist leaves in an ambulance.

The Judge rules on two cases in this episode. Up first, while attending a friend's birthday party, a teenager accidentally breaks an outdoor sprinkler. Her actions, caught on security footage, cause $9K in flooding throughout an apartment building. In the next case, after inheriting her late brother's home, a woman triples the rent on his remaining tenant and sues him for alleged property damage.
In this two-part episode, a woman who suffered abuse as a child is convinced her neighbor is guilty of neglect and reports her to DCS multiple times.
In part two, the Judge must decide if a woman's allegations are justified as feuding neighbors sue for the 10k court maximum over an alleged assault and shocking charges of child endangerment.

Former army buddies pool their resources to purchase one luxury vehicle in order to start a car rental business. A doomed rental ends with the vehicle being wrecked, their insurance being dropped and thousands in damage.

A young widow with a newborn baby claims her deceased husband’s best friend stole money from his account. The best friend defends his actions passionately and says the money went to a GoFundMe set up for his children.
To make ends meet, young parents decide to sell their pets. They immediately regret their decision and fight for the return of one of their dogs.
To compensate for lost playing time during Covid, a devoted father pays a basketball coach $8500 to start up a team for his son. He sues for damages when the team falls apart.

A man claims he was falsely arrested after a road rage incident in which he was accused of wielding a gun. The victim of his alleged fury submits her frantic 911 call claiming a gunshot can be heard in the background.
A battle of bad online reviews is waged in rural Michigan between a pet daycare business and a water supply company.

Her Honor presides over two cases in this episode. In the first, divorcees fight over the fate of $10k in tools: he says she had no right to sell his deceased father's equipment; she says the mortgage had to be paid, and they only sold for $1K. Up next, "Dulce" the Goldendoodle puppy suffers a broken leg while in the care of a new dog sitter who is accused of leaving the pet alone with a child.
Estranged parents fight over their teenager's cell phone, sporting events and a trip to Portugal.

In this two-part episode, a woman does her boss a favor by dropping off lunch to her home only to be attacked by her pit bull the moment she steps through the doorway. The terrifying attack is caught on video.
In part two, after a pit-bull attack, the dog's owner insists that the victim was given fair warning and told not to enter the home.

While riding a scooter together, a man and his son are hit by a truck and thrown to the ground; the father sues the driver for damages but soon finds himself in the hot seat over his handling of the scooter.
After a failed attempt at living together, sisters fight over property damage and the alleged theft of over $14k from their grandmother's inheritance.

In this episode, the Judge rules on two cases. Up first, a German Shepherd digs under a fence, enters a neighbor's house and kills their baby Macaw. The dog’s owner says they should have had a stronger fence. In the next case, a woman faces an uphill battle trying to collect on a loan from her granddaughter's father. The Judge is appalled by how he treats the woman raising his 12-year-old child.

A youth baseball umpire sues for the $10K court maximum after being violently attacked by a coach whose team was disqualified for fielding illegal players. The umpire's son stepped in to defend his father, only to become the target of an attack by angry parents.

The Judge rules on two cases in this episode. First, a woman sues a motorist for destroying her parked vehicle in a catastrophic five-car accident. Video reveals the harrowing collision, the near-death of a pedestrian and the car at fault. Next, after the tragic death of her daughter, a grandmother sues her ex daughter-in-law over money raised at a spaghetti fundraiser for her grandchildren.
A 20-year-old with four young children seeks emotional distress compensation when an acquaintance of her incarcerated husband allegedly embarks on a campaign of harassment and defamation.

When a relationship ends, a woman seeks payback of money loaned to help her ex-boyfriend in his custody battle. He countersues, claiming she sent a doctored video to his workplace that got him fired and orchestrated a smear campaign that jeopardized his parental rights.

The Judge rules on two cases in this episode. First, after four weeks of dating, a woman is persuaded to invest $10K in a car-flipping venture. She fights to recover her investment when the relationship ends, and the business fails. Next, a man drives cross country to help an entrepreneur sell her beard-care products at a fair. Their collaboration ends in a battle over 78 jars of merchandise.
When jealousy sparks a heated argument between two women vying for the same man, a legal battle ensues, fueled by car vandalism and escalating threats.
A contentious landlord-tenant dispute escalates when two men file dueling restraining orders and sue each other over a security deposit, emotional distress, and harassment.

A jointly-owned vehicle is at the center of the conflict between a man and his current and past girlfriend, both of whom share children with him. Missed payments, insurance lapses, and damages from an accident further complicate the dispute.
In this two-part episode, a disabled veteran turned music entrepreneur sues one of 'Atlanta’s top performers’ for the $10K court maximum.

In part two, a music entrepreneur alleges assault and defamation and considers her partnership with a dancer/singer from Atlanta as the biggest mistake of her life. Their doomed dog-breeding venture comes into play.

A seasoned businesswoman and an animal lover dispute the sale of prized miniature pigs. When one piglet dies in transit, and another succumbs shortly after arrival, the absence of a signed contract complicates their legal battle.

The Judge rules on two cases in this episode. First, following an honorable discharge from the military, a teen seeks refuge with her aunt. Months later, she is labeled a ‘burden’ and decides to move out. She sues for belongings left behind. Next, a dog lover is devastated when she entrusts 5 dogs to her groomer but only 4 are returned to her. She is told the dog ‘escaped’ and sues for damages.

In a violent road rage incident, a terrified motorist accuses a driver of deliberately smashing his car window as he attempted to flee the scene after bumping the other car. The defendant claims self-defense, alleging the plaintiff struck him with his car and broke his hand. Both parties submit video footage of the confrontation.

A man seeks $10K in damages for emotional distress after his neighbor's two Cane Corsos injure his German Shepherd. The neighbor claims that the plaintiff's dog started the fight and countersues for $10K, arguing that he was bitten while attempting to separate the dogs.
When little fish Kevin is swept up in a net and taken from his home in the vast oceans to the small glass fish tank of a restaurant, he must find a way to escape and make his way back home.
Frankie and Sophie challenge newcomers Zac and Charlie to an epic sled race.
A teenage boy journeys to find his missing father only to discover that he's actually Bigfoot.

The lovable Ozzy’s pampered life is thrown into turmoil after his family drops him at Blue Creek before their vacation. Ozzy quickly learns that Blue Creek is a dog prison and he’ll need to rely on some new friends to help him break out and get back home.
A loyal dog and a vigilante cat embark on a space age voyage to find their way home.

A rookie race-car driver gets the opportunity to compete against the reigning champion. With help from a former driver, he must overcome treacherous terrain, rival racers and unexpected obstacles to prove he has what it takes.

A cat named Blanket lives in the city with his son, Cape. One day, Cape decides to leave home and embarks on an adventure to find the legendary cat's paradise. To find his son, Blanket must overcome his fear and reconcile with his past.
When his beloved Queen bee Marguerite is kidnapped, vagabond cricket Apollo who has been framed for the crime, teams up with the other bugs to save the Queen and the entire kingdom.
A boy at risk of being sent to boarding school by his Dad - and three aliens stranded due to watching too much TV - must help each other out.

After purchasing a mysterious shrink ray machine, Vick accidentally shrinks Briar, Bramble, and himself. The tiny team must put aside their differences and embark on one big journey to restore their size and their friendship.

In the international race to the moon, the Norwegian mission is led by brilliant inventor Reodor from the village of Flaklypa. With Louis the Magpie as the brave astronaut, what could possibly go wrong? Quite a bit, actually – on the daring mission, secret passengers are discovered, hidden agendas are revealed, and nothing seems to work out the way it was planned. Louis and his friend Luca the Hedgehog are in for some surprises on their trip to the moon. The third film in the stop-motion trilogy

Four crazy anti-heroes, one pawsome adventure. Join special-agent Marnie and her friends as they team up and fight crime. Spoiled and innocent, chubby house cat Marnie lives a comfortable and pampered life in the Sunshine household. She has never ventured outside the family home and only knows about the real world through her favourite detective, crime TV-shows.

Freddy Lupin manages to convince the pack elders to let him sit Howlington Academy’s entrance test. Freddy must use all his poodle wits- and his best friend Batty’s help!- to win a place at the historically wolf-only academy.

It’s the first day of school, and Freddy immediately comes into conflict with bully Ivan, who blackmails him into stealing the sacred moonstone! But when Batty is exposed to the moonstone, she’s turned into a human girl!

Freddy attempts to teach Batty how to be human, while searching for a cure for her new form. A class assignment to capture the mysterious ‘Golden Horn’ and prove who the ‘alpha’ wolf is goes awry when a wilderwolf attacks!

Freddy becomes convinced that there’s a wilderwolf at Howlington, and launches a daring investigation to prove that it’s the school accountant, Mr Sminch. Howlington gets a new teacher, the super cool and charming Ric Rawls.

The kids are struck down by a flea infestation, and Freddy and Batty are tasked with tracking down the mysterious Doog, keeper of the Fleaminator, the most powerful flea treatment known to dog, before they’re all expelled!

The kids head out on their first excursion to Night Patrol HQ. Freddy gets pulled into Scarlet’s world as she gets closer to the truth about werewolves and the two bond when they get stuck in the forest while tracking a wolf.

It’s Howloween, and Howlington is on lockdown. But when the students stage a play that goes wrong and the lockdown is disrupted, it will be up to the kids to save the grown-ups from themselves - including Principal Pincus!

Freddy and Ivan have failed their runes exam and have to do it over - or they won’t be allowed to attend the Doom Wolves concert. But their study session ends up putting themselves, and the Doom Wolves, in grave danger!
When little fish Kevin is swept up in a net and taken from his home in the vast oceans to the small glass fish tank of a restaurant, he must find a way to escape and make his way back home.
Frankie and Sophie challenge newcomers Zac and Charlie to an epic sled race.
A teenage boy journeys to find his missing father only to discover that he's actually Bigfoot.
